entry: Indian actress who appears in [[Hindi]] films. Described in the media as one of the most successful and versatile actresses of Hindi cinema, she debuted in *Bekhudi* (1992) and became a leading star of the 1990s with *Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge* (1995) and *Kuch Kuch Hota Hai* (1998). After a sabbatical from full-time acting, she returned with *Tanhaji* (2020). Kajol is also a social activist, known for her work with widows and children. She has been married to actor [[Ajay Devgn]] since 1999.

Brazilian former professional footballer and attacking midfielder. He spent six years at [[AC Milan]] from 2003, winning the [[Serie A]] title in his first season and leading the club to the 2006–07 [[UEFA Champions League]] as the tournament's top goalscorer. He also won the 2007 Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year. He was in Brazil's squad that won the 2002 [[FIFA World Cup]]. After a transfer to Real Madrid in 2009, he retired in 2017.

Semiarid sandy savanna in [[Southern Africa]], covering 900,000 sq km (350,000 sq mi), including much of [[Botswana]] and parts of [[Namibia]] and [[South Africa]]. Its name derives from the Tswana word *kgala*, meaning "the great thirst." Being a semi-desert, it supports more animals and plants than a true desert, such as the Namib Desert to the west. The driest areas usually receive 110–200 mm (4.3–7.9 in) of rain per year, while summers are very hot. The only permanent river, the Okavango, forms a marshy delta in the northwest, and large salt pans lie across the region, including the Makgadikgadi Pan in Botswana and the Etosha Pan in Namibia. During parts of the late Pleistocene the region was much wetter and cooler, with large paleolakes and river systems.

Form of [[Cabbage|cabbage]] (*Brassica oleracea*) grown chiefly for its edible leaves, which may be curly, flat, or bumpy and range from green to purple. Kale is also grown as an ornamental plant. It originated in the eastern Mediterranean and [[Anatolia]], where it was cultivated by 2000 BCE at the latest. Curly-leaved and flat-leaved varieties both existed in [[Greece]] in the 4th century BC. The plant is hardy and can survive temperatures as low as −15 °C (5 °F), and it can become sweeter after a heavy frost. Russian traders introduced Russian kale into Canada and then the United States in the 19th century. Raw kale is 84% water and provides 207 kilojoules (49 kilocalories) of food energy per 100 g.

Hindu goddess associated with time, death, and destruction. Kali is the first of the ten *Mahavidyas*, goddesses who grant liberating knowledge, and is held to be the most famous of the numerous Hindu goddesses. She is the consort of [[Shiva]]. Her most famous appearance is in the 6th-century CE text *Devi Mahatmya*, where she is the personification of the rage of [[Durga]] and defeats the demon Raktabija, who could reproduce himself from every drop of blood that reached the ground. Kali is worshipped as the Divine Mother, especially in [[Bengal]], and Shakta and Tantric traditions regard her as the ultimate reality, or [[Brahman]]. Her terrifying iconography embodies the grim realities of blood, death, and destruction, and in modern times she has become a significant symbol for women.

Last and shortest of the four *yugas*, or world ages, in Hindu cosmology, and considered the worst. It is believed to be the present age, marked by conflict and sin. Puranic sources date its start to the death of [[Krishna]], at midnight on 17/18 February 3102 BCE (Julian), and its length to 432,000 years. Near its end, a cataclysm is expected to restore [[Dharma|dharma]] and usher in a new Krita (Satya) Yuga, as prophesied by [[Kalki]].

Classical Sanskrit poet and playwright, often considered ancient India's greatest. His name means "servant of [[Kali]]." His surviving works, based largely on Hindu Puranas and philosophy, include three plays, among them *Abhijñānaśākuntalam*; two epic poems, including *Raghuvaṃśa*; and shorter lyric poems such as *Meghadūta*. Scholars place his activity in the late 4th to early 5th century, traditionally linked to the court of [[Chandragupta II]] of the [[Gupta Empire]]. Little is known of his life, and his works were most likely composed before the 5th century CE. They were among the first to gain global recognition through translation: Sir William Jones's 1789 translation of *Abhijñānaśākuntalam* inspired Goethe and European Romantics.

Russian port city (pop., 2020: 489,359), administrative center of [[Kaliningrad Oblast]]. Founded in 1255 by the [[Teutonic Order|Teutonic Knights]] as Königsberg, it became a major Prussian city. It was heavily damaged in [[World War II]] and captured by the [[Soviet Union]] on 9 April 1945. It was renamed Kaliningrad in 1946, after the Bolshevik leader Mikhail Kalinin. The city is the headquarters of Russia's Baltic Fleet and one of the largest industrial centers in Russia.

Westernmost federal subject of [[Russia]], a semi-exclave on the [[Baltic Sea]] bordered by [[Poland]] and [[Lithuania]]. Covering 15,125 sq km (5,840 sq mi), it had a population of roughly one million in the 2021 census, and its largest city is [[Kaliningrad]]. The territory was formerly the northern part of East Prussia, inhabited mainly by Germans. The [[Teutonic Order]] conquered the region in the 13th century. After [[Nazi Germany]]'s defeat in [[World War II]], the Soviet Union annexed it, and the flight and expulsion of Germans left the area largely unpopulated. It was then resettled mainly by Soviet citizens, chiefly ethnic Russians, who form its dominant population today.

Prophesied tenth and final [[Avatar|avatar]] of the Hindu god [[Vishnu]]. He is expected to appear at the end of the [[Kali Yuga]] to end its darkest period of adharma, restore [[Dharma|dharma]], and begin the Satya Yuga. In the Puranas he rides a white horse named Devadatta and wields a fiery sword. The name may derive from *karki*, meaning white, which refers to the horse. Kalki also appears in the Kalachakra-Tantra of Tibetan [[Buddhism]] and in Sikh texts.

Ancient Sanskrit text on love, desire, and emotional fulfillment, attributed to Vātsyāyana. It is not chiefly a sex manual but a guide to the art of living well, covering courtship, partners, and married life. Historians date it variously between 400 BCE and 300 CE. It influenced later texts and Indian art, including reliefs in temples such as Khajuraho in [[Madhya Pradesh]]. According to Wendy Doniger, Richard Burton's 1883 English edition, the first European one, was revised to suit Victorian tastes.

Indian actor, filmmaker, and politician who works primarily in Tamil cinema. He has made over 230 films in several Indian languages and began as a child actor, winning a Rashtrapati Award at age six for *Kalathur Kannamma*. In 2018 he founded the political party Makkal Needhi Maiam, and in 2007 he was appointed a [[United Nations]] ambassador for a campaign protecting the rights of people living with [[HIV]]. He was sworn into the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Indian Parliament, in 2025.

American politician and attorney who served as the 49th vice president of the United States from 2021 to 2025 under [[Joe Biden]]. A member of the Democratic Party, she was the first female, first African American, and first Asian American vice president. She was attorney general of [[California]] from 2011 to 2017 and a U.S. senator from 2017 to 2021. As vice president she cast 33 tie-breaking Senate votes, more than any other vice president. She was the Democratic nominee in the 2024 presidential election, losing to [[Donald Trump]], who won 312 electoral votes to her 226.

Peninsula in the Russian Far East, between the [[Sea of Okhotsk]] and the [[Bering Sea]]. It forms part of Kamchatka Krai, and more than half of its population lives in the port city of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, on Avacha Bay. Two mountain ranges, the Sredinny Range and the Eastern Range, run along its length. The peninsula contains the volcanoes of Kamchatka, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that forms part of the [[Ring of Fire]]. Klyuchevskaya Sopka, an isolated volcanic group in the central valley, is Eurasia's highest active volcano, at 4,750 metres. Snow covers the peninsula from October to late May, and the Valley of Geysers lies within the Kronotsky Biosphere Reserve.

Conqueror and first ruler of the Kingdom of [[Hawaii]], also known as Kamehameha the Great. By 1795 he had conquered Maui, Lānaʻi, Molokaʻi, and Oʻahu, and full unification of the [[Hawaiian Islands]] came in 1810, when Kauaʻi and Niʻihau submitted peacefully. He used Western firearms and vessels acquired through trade to gain military advantage. As king he centralized governance, promulgated the Law of the Splintered Paddle to protect civilians in wartime, and fostered economic ties with foreign powers. His line, the Kamehameha Dynasty, ruled until 1872. The state of Hawaii gave a statue of him to the National Statuary Hall Collection in [[Washington, D.C.]]

Capital and largest city of [[Uganda]] (pop., 2024: 1,797,722), near the northern shore of [[Lake Victoria]]. The city proper is divided into five political divisions. In 2015 its metropolitan area generated an estimated nominal GDP of $13.8 billion (constant US dollars of 2011), more than half of Uganda's GDP for that year. Estimates of the metropolitan population range from around four million to 6,709,900 in 2019. The name is a local rendering of "Hill of the [[Impala]]," the British name for Old Kampala hill, a royal hunting reserve of the Kabaka of Buganda where colonial officials built Fort Lugard. The consulting firm Mercer has regularly ranked Kampala as East Africa's best city to live in, ahead of [[Nairobi]] and [[Kigali]].

Japanese judoka, educator, and politician who founded [[Judo|judo]] and established the Kodokan Judo Institute in [[Tokyo]] in 1882. Judo was one of the first Japanese martial arts to gain international recognition, and it has been an official Olympic sport since 1964 for men and 1992 for women. Kanō introduced black and white belts and dan ranking. He was director of primary education in the Ministry of Education from 1898 to 1901 and president of Tokyo Higher Normal School from 1900 to 1920. As the first Asian member of the International Olympic Committee, serving from 1909 to 1938, he represented Japan at most Olympic Games from 1912 to 1936. He also helped introduce and systematize [[Karate|karate]] in Japan. His mottoes included "maximum efficiency minimal effort" and "mutual welfare and benefit."

City in southern [[Afghanistan]] and capital of Kandahar Province, at about 1,010 m (3,310 ft) above sea level between the Arghandab and Tarnak rivers. A fortified city existed on the site by c. 1000–750 BC, and [[Alexander the Great]] laid the foundation of Old Kandahar in the 4th century BC, naming it Alexandria Arachosia. In 1747 [[Ahmad Shah Durrani]] made Kandahar the capital of the Durrani Empire. It has been the traditional seat of the [[Pashtuns|Pashtun]] people for more than 300 years and is a center of trade and fruit production, notably figs, grapes, and pomegranates. Kandahar is the founding city and spiritual center of the [[Taliban]], where the group's supreme leader is based, although the Taliban maintain Kabul as the official capital.

Empire based around [[Lake Chad]] in Africa, c. 700–1902. [[Trans-Saharan trade]] sustained it, and the empire exported salt, ivory, slaves, and animal products. It is among the oldest and longest-lived empires in African history. In the 11th century the empire converted to [[Islam]], and it reached the peak of its power under *mai* Idris IV Alooma in the late 16th century. Decline began in the 17th century. In 1893 the Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr conquered the empire, and its territories were incorporated into French, British, and German colonial empires in 1902. Remnants survive in the non-sovereign Borno and Dikwa emirates of [[Nigeria]].

Large [[Marsupial|marsupial]] of the family Macropodidae, native to [[Australia (continent)|Australia]] and [[New Guinea]]. The term usually denotes the largest species, such as the red kangaroo and the eastern grey kangaroo. A large male can be 2 metres (6 feet 7 inches) tall and weigh 90 kg (200 lb). Kangaroos have large, powerful hind legs and feet adapted for leaping, and females carry their young in a pouch. Their molars wear down and move forward before being replaced, a process called polyphyodonty that among mammals occurs only in [[Elephant|elephants]] and [[Manatee|manatees]]. The kangaroo appears on Australia's coat of arms and as the logo of [[Qantas]]. An estimated 42.8 million kangaroos lived in Australia's commercial harvest areas in 2019, down from 53.2 million in 2013.

Third-highest mountain in the world, at 8,586 m (28,169 ft) on the border of [[Nepal]] and the Indian state of [[Sikkim]], in the [[Himalayas]]. Until 1852 it was assumed to be the highest, but survey measurements showed that [[Mount Everest]] is higher, and it was officially ranked third in 1856. The mountain is sacred in Nepal and Sikkim. It was first climbed on 25 May 1955 by Joe Brown and George Band, who stopped short of the true summit, keeping a promise to the Chogyal of Sikkim. The adjoining Khangchendzonga National Park became a [[World Heritage Site]] in 2016.

Emperor of China's [[Qing dynasty]] from 1661 to 1722, whose reign of 61 years is the longest in Chinese history. After taking personal control in 1669, he suppressed the Revolt of the Three Feudatories and forced the Kingdom of Tungning in Taiwan and the Mongols to submit to Qing rule. He incorporated [[Tibet]] into the empire. His reign brought long-term stability and began the High Qing era, which spanned his reign and those of his son Yongzheng and grandson Qianlong. The court compiled the *Kangxi Dictionary* and the *Complete Tang Poems* anthology. He initially welcomed [[Jesuits]], but tolerance ended after the Chinese Rites controversy.

Kushan emperor, c. 127–150 CE, whose reign marked the zenith of the [[Kushan Empire]]. His empire extended from [[Central Asia]] and Gandhara to Pataliputra in the Gangetic plains. Its main capital was at Puruṣapura ([[Peshawar]]) in Gandhara, with another major capital at Mathura. Although he never converted to [[Buddhism]], his conquests and patronage of Buddhism helped spread [[Mahayana]] Buddhism from Gandhara across the Karakoram range to [[China]] and played an important role in the development of the [[Silk Road]]. Around 127 CE he replaced Greek with Bactrian as the language of administration. Earlier scholars dated his accession to 78 CE, but historians no longer accept that date.

Logographic [[Chinese characters]] used in writing Japanese, alongside the syllabic scripts [[Hiragana]] and [[Katakana]]. Significant use of Chinese characters in Japan began around the 5th century AD, and nearly 3,000 kanji are used in names and common communication. Most kanji have two readings: *on'yomi*, derived from Chinese pronunciation, and *kun'yomi*, based on native Japanese. After the [[Meiji Restoration]], Japan simplified many characters into *shinjitai*, or new character forms, to increase literacy.

Dravidian language spoken predominantly in [[Karnataka]], southwestern [[India]], where it is the official and administrative language. It has 44 million native speakers, and the 2011 census counted 43.7 million native speakers in India. Early Kannada literature was composed largely by Jain court poets, and the language has an unbroken literary history of around 1,500 years. It was the court language of several dynasties, including the Kadamba, Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Hoysala, and [[Vijayanagara Empire]]. Written in a script that evolved from the 5th-century Kadamba script, Kannada has been considerably influenced by [[Sanskrit]] in its grammar and vocabulary. A center for the study of classical Kannada was established in Mysore in July 2011.
